precepts.text: Let the day perish wherein I was born. This is how the Hebrews felt regarding birthdays.
precepts.point: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
precepts.why:
Joseph's interpretations came to pass “the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants.” On that birthday “he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again,” “But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.”

Wherever you read of a birthday in scripture, Pharaoh's birthday, Herod's birthday, the birthday of one of the Greek kings, something bad happens. Here a man is hanged at a birthday feast. A birthday is a day of narcissism, a day of proclaiming yourself to be God.

Job shows how the Hebrews felt about the day of their birth: “Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.” A righteous man did not exalt the day he was born; he wished it would perish. That is why we never celebrated birthdays.

precepts.text: Why died I not from the womb?
precepts.point: Solomon praised the dead more than the living; Job wished he had died from the womb. The comfort is in the scriptures.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
Because of verse 1, with no comforter and all the power on the side of our oppressors, Solomon says: “Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.” Better than both is he “which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.” He would rather praise the dead, who are not going through the oppression, than the living, who are depressed, oppressed, suppressed, pressed all kinds of ways.

Job said the same: “Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Job was going through tribulation hell: his wife on him, his kids dying, the skin disease, his lands, everything lost. Why didn't I just die already? Why am I still here?

“For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest”. If he had slept, meaning been dead, he would have been at rest, not going through the hell he was going through; or as “infants which never saw light”, meaning stillborn. “There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.” We are the prisoners. In death they don't have to deal with oppressors no more.

That is how heavy the oppression of Ecclesiastes 4:1 is. And the only reason we are still breathing is the mercy of the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
Job is the precept that there is no inquisition in the grave. Job was catching so much hell that he said “Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Why didn’t I die as a baby? His kids got put to death, he lost all his businesses, he got sick, all kinds of plagues were on his flesh, and his wife was a nag getting on his nerves.

“Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?” The knees are the mother rocking a baby on her knees to keep it up and about. “For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest”, “with kings and counsellors of the earth”, “or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver”, “or as an hidden untimely birth”: a still birth, “as infants which never saw light.”

“There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.” The prisoners are our people, at rest together in death. “The small and great are there”, in the grave, at rest, “and the servant is free from his master.”

So when we die, brothers and sisters, we are all at rest, whether you are righteous or you are wicked as hell.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
Once we come into the truth it’s not going to be a smooth ride at all. “For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me”. Job was keeping God’s laws, but he understood that evil will come: there will be a rainy day and a sunny day. He kept that in the back of his mind. Even though he kept the laws, he knew the Lord can put him in any situation if he pleases.

“I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.” He wasn’t comfortable. He knew the Lord can change his circumstances at any time, so he didn’t put his feet up and just chill. Yet trouble came. Trouble will come; that’s it.

moments.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day. Why did he curse his day? Because his children were celebrating their day, and Job cursed the day he was born.

Job is going in on his birthday. That is why we say to hell with our birthday, our birthday means nothing. The scriptures say better is the day of one's death than the day of one's birth, because when you are born there are no works yet; when you die that is when people remember your works and what kind of person you were.

Job said, let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, there is a man child conceived; let that day be darkness, let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it, let a cloud dwell upon it, let the blackness of the day terrify it; as for that night, let darkness seize upon it, let it not be joined unto the days of the year.

Let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein, let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning. Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none.

Because it shut not up the doors of my mother's womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes. Job is not cursing anything else but his birth right here; all the stuff he is going through, he is saying, man, I just should have never been born.
Why died I not from the womb? Why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly? Job said I should have died at my birth, I should have died stillborn, I should have died in the womb.

For now I should have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept, then had I been at rest, with kings and counsellors of the earth. Or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants which never saw light. He is talking about miscarriages: why wasn't I miscarried, why did I have to come into this world?

There the wicked cease from troubling. When wicked people die, that is it, they can do no more wrong. When Esau is dead the earth is not going to be troubled anymore. There the prisoners rest together, they hear not the voice of the oppressor.

This is why in New Orleans there is a celebration when people die; they call it a second line, and it goes all the way back to slave times. They are celebrating the fact that the prisoners rest together and hear not the voice of the oppressor; they are celebrating that they are not in slavery anymore.
The small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master. Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul?

Which long for death, but it cometh not, and dig for it more than for hid treasures. It has got to be some serious trouble and anguish that you are in for you to only think about dying. Some of us have gone through situations where we would rather just be dead, but sometimes we go through things like that in order to be stronger.

Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad when they can find the grave. If you have had a grandmother or aunt or uncle that was very old, going to dialysis, getting blood transfusions and chemo, after a while they are ready to leave, ready to go. The scriptures say death is better than continual sickness.

Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in? For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters. For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me.

I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came. It was not like everything was going hunky dory for Job; he was already going through some stuff, and trouble came anyway. He is saying, man, what am I doing wrong?
Every verse here is about death: what happens when we die. Job was catching hell. He lost his businesses, his children’s homes, his children’s lives, his health. He lost everything.
“Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Why wasn’t I born dead? A stillbirth, they call it.

“Why did the knees prevent me?” When a baby is born, the mother rocks the baby, stimulating it, continuously rocking. “Or why the breasts that I should suck?” The baby has to suckle the breast to stay nourished.
Had he died before he was born, he says, “should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest.”

Notice who is at rest: “kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves”, “Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver.” Kings have died, counsellors have died, princes have died, and they are all at rest.
“Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been”: that is the stillborn, “as infants which never saw light.”
“There the wicked cease from troubling.” Notice that: in death even the wicked cease from troubling. “And there the weary be at rest.”
Even in death “the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.”
“The small and great are there”: the small of the nations and the great of the nations. “And the servant is free from his master.”
From verse 11 down to 19 Job is saying that when everybody dies, they are at rest. There is no torment, no arguing, no oppression, no weariness. Everybody is at rest.

Now we’re getting into the topic: we’re going to talk about death. “Why died I not from the womb?” Why didn’t I die as a baby? “Why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Why didn’t I die when I was born? Job caught hell, so he’s upset.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “Why did the knees prevent me?” Why my mama’s knees, my family: how your mama bounces you on her knees as a baby to keep you up and keep you going. “Or why the breasts that I should suck?” Why was she giving me her breasts to feed me, breastfeed me, nurture me.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “For now should I have lain still and been quiet”: if my mama didn’t do that, I would have laid still and dead. “I should have slept: then had I been at rest”: if I died I would have been at rest.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: At rest “with kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves; Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver”.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “An hidden untimely birth”: that’s stillborn deaths. Why was I not like that, “as infants which never saw light.”

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: There, when you’re dead, “the wicked cease from troubling” people, “and there the weary be at rest.”

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “There the prisoners rest together” in the grave. “They hear not the voice of the oppressor”: there’s no oppressor when you’re dead.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “The small and great are there”: the small of the nations are there and the greatest of the nations are there, “and the servant is free from his master.”

Job is explaining death. When you die your soul, your spirit, is at rest. You’re not being thrown in the middle of the earth with Satan saying gotcha now, gotcha, gotcha, poking you with a pitchfork. But when Christ comes, that’s another matter.
